summary.headline: Chemplast Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA loss of INR115 crores on INR1,125 crores revenue; net loss INR176 crores on VCM high-cost inventory.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue rose to INR1,125 crores from INR1,100 crores a year earlier, but input cost spikes from the Middle East disruption drove an EBITDA loss of INR115 crores and a net loss of INR176 crores. Management attributed the loss mainly to high-priced VCM inventory booked around March-April, which it says will be consumed by July-August. Specialty chemicals (CMCD) volumes grew 21% YoY and the segment is described as recovering, while Suspension PVC and caustic/chloromethane remained under price pressure. Management expects spreads near $160/t from September onward, with the Karaikal PVC plant offline after a 17 July fire.

segments.name: Suspension PVC
segments.commentary: Revenue INR569 crores vs INR608 crores YoY; prices fell in April after duty exemption let Chinese imports surge, and demand softened seasonally. Management guides spread to ~$160/t (India, replacement basis) from September.

segments.name: Paste PVC
segments.commentary: Realisations about $200/t above Suspension PVC per management; Cuddalore 7,000 t debottlenecking on track for October 2026 commissioning.

segments.name: Specialty / CMCD
segments.commentary: Volumes up 21% YoY on revenue of INR427 crores; 14 molecules commercial out of ~50 in pipeline; INR1,000 crore revenue target reiterated as on track. MPB-3 Phase 3 and pilot Phase 3 commissioned; utilisation ex-new assets ~60-70%.

segments.name: Refrigerant gas (R32)
segments.commentary: Commercial production started May 2026 from swing plant; full 14,000 t capacity expected online by end of FY27 per management, with ramp-up in Q4 FY27 and Q1 FY28.

segments.name: Value-added chemicals (caustic, chloromethane, H2O2)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR129 crores vs INR138 crores; lower output due to planned caustic membrane changeover; caustic pricing under pressure from weak demand and excess supply.

guidance_outlook: Management expects VCM high-cost inventory to be consumed by July and part of August, with normal-price VCM from September and better Q3 performance.
Targeted spread of ~$160/t between PVC and VCM; management says ~$120-130/t needed for EBITDA neutral and a further ~$20-30/t for PBT positive.
Management declined to give a numerical guidance but said 'reasonable performance' expected from Q3 FY27.
Onerous contract net provisions of ~INR90 crores (CCVL) and ~INR30 crores (Chemplast) expected to be reversed in Q2 FY27.
R32 full capacity expected online by end of FY27; management says margin contribution is healthy but too early to forecast sustainability.
Debottlenecking of 7,000 t at Cuddalore Paste PVC due October 2026.
capex_capacity: Karaikal PVC plant manually shut after a fire on 17 July 2026; no injuries or spillage reported; restoration timeline not disclosed on the call.
Cuddalore Paste PVC 7,000 t debottlenecking on track for October 2026.
CMCD: MPB-3 Phase 3 and pilot Phase 3 commissioned in Q1 FY27; CMCD capacity expanded from ~1,100 t to ~5,400 t per analyst question (not contested).
R32: 14,000 t capacity targeted online by end of FY27; swing plant commercial production from May 2026.
Caustic soda capacity 120,000 t, operating range 100-120k t given electrolyser ageing.
demand_pricing: Paste PVC demand recovered to 70-80% downstream operating rates in June as Middle East situation eased; Europe and Asia supplies turned aggressive from mid-June.
Suspension PVC prices fell in April; customs duty on PVC resin exempted 2 April-30 June 2026 and reinstated 16 July 2026; minimum import price (MIP) imposed for six months.
Anti-dumping recommendation on EU and Japan Paste PVC imports lapsed; Madras High Court ordered provisional assessment and importer bonds for retrospective ADD recovery.
Agchem market subdued with generic competition from China; management says demand on commercialised molecules remains healthy but some ramp-ups delayed by a quarter.
Caustic soda and chloromethane prices under pressure from weak regional demand and excess supply; hydrogen peroxide volumes up sequentially.

qa_highlights.question: What is the VCM sourcing situation and would the company partially shut the plant given negative economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Replacement VCM ~$700/t delivered vs PVC ~$900+/t, a $150-160 spread; management is evaluating alternate VCM sources and expects VCM prices to soften further.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q1 PVC-VCM spread and what spread is needed for EBITDA and PBT breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 spread was negative (VCM ~$1,000+/t landed vs realisation ~$700-750/t). EBITDA neutral needs ~$120-130/t; PBT positive needs another $20-30/t.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company locked into fixed-price PVC contracts with floating raw material costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contracts are formula/market-linked on both PVC and VCM; the Q1 loss came from VCM parcels booked at March peak prices when PVC prices later fell.

qa_highlights.question: How concentrated is CMCD revenue across the 14 commercial molecules and is the INR1,000 crore target agchem-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is mostly agchem and spread across multiple customers and innovators; management declined to give product or customer concentration. The INR1,000 crore target is reflective of agchem molecules already commercialised; pharma and other specialty projects are not included.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CMCD utilisation and ROCE trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Excluding the newly commissioned MPB-3 Phase 3, utilisation is ~60-70%; management expects returns to reach industry levels this year as costs optimise.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company plan to service debt with ~INR235 crores annual interest and negative FCF from growth capex?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said conserved cash and current accruals will cover debt servicing; liquidity is sufficient and no equity dilution flagged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the spread for Paste vs Suspension PVC?
qa_highlights.answer: Paste realisations are ~$200/t above Suspension PVC per management.

risks_watch: Whether the high-cost VCM inventory is fully consumed by August and the ~$160/t PVC-VCM spread actually materialises from September, as management guided.
Karaikal PVC plant offline after the 17 July 2026 fire; restoration timeline was not disclosed on the call and volume impact on Q2 is unquantified.
Durability of the policy support: customs duty on PVC resin reinstated 16 July 2026 and MIP for six months; ADD on EU/Japan Paste PVC lapsed and depends on Madras High Court proceedings.
R32 14,000 t capacity targeted fully online by end-FY27 with partnerships still under discussion; management said it is too early to forecast R32 margin sustainability.
Onerous contract net provision of about INR90 crores (CCVL) and INR30 crores (Chemplast) expected to reverse in Q2 FY27, and the earlier INR150 crore provision description was unclear on the call.
Debt servicing with interest near INR235 crores a year and negative free cash flow from growth capex; management relied on conserved cash and accruals without quantifying the cash break-even.
key_quotes: The VCM high -priced inventory that we had booked, which was close to $1,000-plus, that affected the first quarter and we will consume everything by July and part of August.
So getting into September and gett ing into Q3, we should be in a better position if the same price levels continue on both sides, whether VCM or PVC.
So I don't want to guide an exact number to you, but I think we should see a reasonable performance from Q3.
So in general, PVC prices is floating and VCM prices are also market driven and they are floating. We don't lock one side and keep the other side open.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the forward PVC spread, CMCD momentum and R32 timelines, but evasive on hard numbers: it declined to give EBITDA or revenue guidance, offering only "reasonable performance" from Q3 FY27. It was defensive on the PVC contract structure and on the negative Q1 spread, attributing the loss to high-priced VCM booked in March.

adds.what: R32 refrigerant gas 14,000 t/yr full capacity (swing plant commercial production started May 2026)
CMCD MPB-3 Phase 3 and pilot Phase 3 capacity (expanded ~1,100 t to ~5,400 t per analyst question, not contested)

growth.why: Management reiterated the INR1,000 crore CMCD revenue target and R32 full 14,000 t capacity by end of FY27, plus a Cuddalore 7,000 t debottlenecking in October 2026, but no numeric revenue guidance was given, Q1 revenue only grew about 2% YoY (INR1,125 vs INR1,100 crore), and the Karaikal PVC plant is offline after a 17 July fire with restoration timing undisclosed.
